prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate having acquired the necessary knowledge to determine the analysis of pneumatic and hydraulic mechanisms, as well as their theoretical and practical resolution.
Know the English vocabulary related to the subject. Analysis and interpretation of an English document related to the subject.

syllabus_topics: Magnitudes and units: Absolute pressure, relative pressure. Perfect gases.
Production and distribution of compressed air. Types of compressors. Compressed air treatment. Filtering, regulation and lubrication.
Actuating elements, cylinders and motors: Type, sizing of the section and rod dimensions. Calculation of air consumption.
Control elements: Distributor valves. Auxiliary valves: non-return, selector, shuttle, flow and pressure regulating, quick exhaust and variable throttling non-return.
Sensors. (Inform about pressure and position to feed the system). Limit switch, flow or air barrier, and pressure switch.

Design of pneumatic circuits. Terminology. Work sequence diagram, spaces and space-time. Principles of command and speed control. Method of systematic cancellation of permanent signals (three or more lines).
Hydraulic fluids: Density, pressure, viscosity, fluidity and lubrication and cooling capacity, emulsivity, corrosion resistance.
Principles of fluid mechanics: Pascal's principles, mass conservation, Bernoulli's theorem. Types of regime: laminar and turbulent. Reynolds number. Fluids in conduits, head losses.
Hydraulic installations: Pressure generators, filters, pressure gauges, tanks, accumulators, pumps (types and parameters).
Distribution, regulation and working elements. Conduits, distributor valves, regulating valves. Actuators (cylinders and motors: gear, vane and piston).
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (1.5 hours per week) with audiovisual aids, printed material, and exercise solving.
Practical classes in the classroom (0.5 hours per week) with practical exercises.
Practical classes in the classroom (1 hour per week) for theory comprehension, including graded seminars and group exercise analysis.
Laboratory practices (15 hours per semester in four 3-hour sessions) for applying concepts and conducting measurements, requiring autonomous report writing.
Group-tutored work to analyze a scientific article in English related to the subject.
Following activities proposed in the Virtual Campus.

assessment_methods.method: Test 1: Performance of real and/or simulated task execution tests

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is a weighted average of four tests (15%, 15%, 20%, 50%), provided a minimum score of 5 out of 10 is obtained in each test. Failure to meet minimum requirements in any test will result in a final grade of 3.5. Practices (Module III) are mandatory and must be passed ("APTO"); if not, an additional development test on practices, requiring a minimum score of 5 out of 10, is necessary. For single assessment, a single written development test accounts for 100% of the grade, requiring a minimum score of 5 out of 10. Practices are considered "APTO" if results are correct, reports are error-free, well-presented, and submitted on time.
